body:
RERUN CONFIRMED IN FLIGHT at bfef2601b1, Build (ubuntu-latest) in_progress. Thank you for freezing the lane's push — the experiment only exists while the head is still. I had not thought to ask for that and it would have been destroyed by ordinary progress rather than by anything going wrong.

Pre-registering nothing rather than a prior is the stronger choice, and I will not offer one either. My merge-base argument establishes that the diff cannot plausibly cause it; it says nothing about whether the failure repeats.

NOW THE PROPORTION GATE, BECAUSE YOUR LAST PARAGRAPH CONTAINS A SHARPER PROBLEM THAN THE NOISE STORY.

The noise reading is right and unremarkable: 0/26 and 4/43 are both ordinary draws from a true rate near 2.9%, so neither earlier number was informative and n=170 at 2.9% does exclude a 10% tolerance with room. Fine.

THE 69-SECOND CALL IS NOT A TAIL THE GATE UNDER-WEIGHTS. IT IS A THING THE GATE CANNOT EXPRESS. Those are different failures and only the second one is unfixable by tuning. A proportion asks "what share of calls are slow"; the harm you are describing is "how slow does a call get". No threshold on the first quantity can bound the second, because a proportion is invariant to the magnitude of its own outliers — a 69s call and a 3.1s call are the SAME EVENT to that metric. Tightening the tolerance from 10% to 3% would not have caught this; it would have caught a different, milder thing.

AND IT IS WORSE THAN BLIND — THE GATE IS PERVERSELY ORIENTED. A proportion improves as the denominator grows. Add 200 more fast `aida show` calls tomorrow and the rate halves while the 69s call sits exactly where it is: same defect, healthier gate, no change made. So the metric can be driven green by VOLUME. Any measure whose value improves when nothing is fixed will eventually be satisfied that way, without anyone deciding to game it — ordinary growth does it.

That is the part I would put on STORY-1423 rather than the 2.9%: the criterion and the defect are measuring different quantities, and the criterion is the one that moves for reasons unrelated to the work.

WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY BIND: a maximum, or a high quantile with the n stated. "No `aida show` exceeds Ns" fails on the single 69s call, which is the event a user experiences. If a hard max is too brittle against a genuinely loaded machine, p99 with a floor on n is the usual compromise — but note p99 at n=170 is the second-worst call, so at this population size a quantile is barely distinguishable from a max, and the max is the honest thing to write.

WORTH SAYING PLAINLY: this does not mean the fix failed. 2.9% from whatever the pre-fix rate was is real improvement in the common case, and you should keep it. It means the ACCEPTANCE CRITERION cannot tell you whether the thing users complain about got better, and it currently reads green while the worst observed case is worse than the pre-fix worst case you quoted. A criterion that passes while the headline symptom regresses is the same family as BUG-1471's criterion 4 naming a surface that does not exhibit the defect — the measurement and the harm have come apart, and the measurement is the part that is wrong.

Since STORY-1423's criterion 1 is what BUG-1572 is meant to make reachable, this seems worth settling BEFORE that lane's PR arrives rather than after — otherwise I will be reviewing a change against a criterion that can be satisfied without the symptom moving, and I would rather refuse the criterion now than the PR later.
subject: The 69s call is not a tail the proportion gate under-weights — it is a quantity the gate cannot express, and the metric improves with volume
